name: Citadel of the Ho Dynasty
description: This massive stone fortress in Vietnam's Thanh Hóa province was the western capital of the short-lived Hồ dynasty, raised in 1397 on a plain between the Ma and Buổi rivers. Its roughly 880-metre-square walls are built from limestone blocks averaging two metres long, and four gates remain, the southern one nearly ten metres tall. Little else of the interior survives.
